decisions.scope: Full replaceable Harness plugins; trusted locally installed third-party processes; built-in Native and Codex; GUI and TUI retain the complete coding workflow; new data model allowed.
architecture: New r-code-harness-protocol owns versioned wire DTOs only (serde/serde_json, no product/platform/Provider implementation dependencies). r-code-kernel owns task/run/attempt state machines and ports; it depends on protocol and neutral libraries only.

New r-code-runtime composes existing Gateway, storage, model providers, MCP, terminal, workspace, review, and external process services without Tauri. Desktop and TUI consume one ApplicationService; TUI must not depend on r-code-host/src-tauri.

New r-code-harness-sdk provides the Rust plugin client/server helper. plugins/native and plugins/codex are separately compiled executable Cargo packages. They use the same stdio protocol/manifest/registry as third-party harnesses; neither can import r-code-runtime, r-code-store, r-code-gateway or Tauri. Existing runtime strategy is ported into the Native plugin; platform/execution/storage services stay host-side.

Keep all new crates in this workspace; no new git submodule or separate repository. Reuse agent-contracts internally through adapters; do not expose its changing product-specific DTOs as the plugin wire contract.

User selected a shared background service. Each dev/production v2 profile has exactly one r-code-service daemon owning SQLite, leases, recovery and all runs. GUI/TUI/MCP are clients; closing a frontend does not stop it. Explicit service stop cancels/drains all work; no automatic idle shutdown in v1.

Add a thin r-code-client crate for local Application RPC. Reuse agent-ipc framing helpers, not its default unauthenticated listener/socket-unlink startup. Use profile-specific Unix sockets (0600) or current-user-only Windows named pipes, owner OS lock, a profile-protected random token, protocol handshake and independent command/event connections. Command calls return durable operation IDs for long work; events.read(after_seq) supports reconnect without duplicate effects.

Application RPC mutations carry (profile_id, client_id)-scoped client-generated command_id separate from plugin attempt operation_key. Clients persist an outbox entry before first send; retry/reconnect uses the same command_id. The daemon persists normalized input hash, acceptance and result atomically; same id/different payload is rejected. This covers task creation, message submission, plugin install, approvals and stop even before any attempt exists.

Client outboxes persist stable client_id/command_id before transmission and retain them until acknowledgement; sensitive settings carry credential-broker references, never plaintext secrets in the outbox. Receipt hashes include method and canonical payload.
plugin_contract: Host-to-plugin methods: initialize, harness.start, harness.resume, harness.steer, harness.cancel, shutdown. Plugin-to-host methods: host.model.stream, host.tools.list/call, host.process.open/write/close, host.context.read, host.artifacts.put/read, host.plan.publish/update, host.questions.ask, host.children.spawn/wait/cancel, host.verification.run, host.checkpoint.save, host.completion.propose. Public progress uses harness.event; model/process streams use correlated notifications.

UTF-8 newline-delimited bidirectional JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdin/stdout. stdout contains protocol only; bounded stderr is diagnostics. Use 1 MiB maximum frames, blob references for larger content/attachments, a 16 MiB aggregate bounded queue, 10s initialize timeout, 5s graceful cancellation then process-tree termination. Long model/tool calls use typed operation deadlines and cancellation, not the control timeout. A separate protocol reader must continue serving callbacks while a request is pending.

Manifest harness.json: schema_version, id, version, api_major/min_minor, display_name, supported_platforms, entrypoint executable+argv per platform, supported_features, requested_host_services, config_schema. Host schema validation, negotiated capabilities and install grants determine the effective service set. A process cannot claim another run identity; the connection binds task/run/generation, all handles are run-scoped.

Local directory or zip install copies into an immutable AppData id/version/content-hash directory; reject path traversal, symlink/reparse escapes, duplicate changed content under an existing identity, missing entrypoint or incompatible protocol. Never auto-execute repository manifests, install hooks, or package-manager commands. Entry executable is package-relative native code (a language runtime may be bundled); launch with argv directly. No marketplace, online auto-update, Rust dylib ABI, WASM, custom plugin UI, or malicious-plugin sandbox in v1.

Pin package digest, configuration hash, capabilities, TaskContract and plugin checkpoint schema for each run. Updates apply to new runs; active or recoverable pinned versions cannot be removed. Each active run has its own process; children use their own runs. Harness switching is allowed only by creating a new branch from an idle task using the canonical transcript and TaskContract; opaque checkpoint state is never moved across harnesses.

Third-party plugins are trusted local programs: host mediation audits host API calls and avoids sending provider secrets, but is not an OS sandbox against direct plugin I/O. Codex uses the generic host process service and its App Server protocol; inner CLI actions are external observations, not falsely recorded as Gateway-enforced actions.

JSON-RPC ids are connection-local correlation only. Every effectful host method has an operation_key stable within attempt_id across generation changes; host stores canonical input hash and result. Safe queries may retry; completed effects replay receipts; file effects reconcile expected hashes; process.open/write and external acknowledgements with uncertain effects become indeterminate. Generation fencing does not erase dedup history.

User inputs have host-generated message_id/input_seq. Plugin checkpoint.save atomically stores opaque state and consumed_input_seq after validating delivered contiguous input. Host queue acceptance is exactly once; delivery to plugins may replay from checkpoint and external CLI application is never claimed exactly once. Lost Codex acknowledgement requires reconciliation or a user-requested new attempt.

Add host.approvals.request only for a host-created pending operation reference; generic host.questions.ask cannot create permission grants or change the TaskContract. Models/tools/checks/process launches share AuthorizationService(OperationDescriptor, TaskContract, WorkspaceCapability, effective permissions). A plugin service grant never authorizes a particular side effect.

Managed processes require host-resolved LaunchCapability, executable/argv/cwd and scoped secret references. Native tools, verification preparation and Codex launch all authorize before an operation intent or spawn. Codex uses a host-interpreted declarative process constraint profile that fixes cwd/sandbox/approval ceilings and validates permission-affecting outbound requests; opaque/raw process profiles are unavailable for read-only/Plan tasks. External inner actions remain explicitly externally controlled.

LaunchCapability uses a neutral ProcessProfile from the pinned plugin package: framing, method allowlist, field constraints and bindings to host-owned workspace/permission values. For NDJSON-RPC profiles, the host buffers complete frames and applies declarative method/JSON-pointer constraints before forwarding bytes; unknown or forbidden methods fail closed. The Codex package supplies its App Server schema/profile, so neither kernel nor generic process service hardcodes Codex method names. Only trusted/installed profiles that declare the needed controls are eligible for restricted task modes; raw profiles require non-restricted authorization.
domain_and_data: TaskContract contains task kind, objective, constraints and required check definitions; WorkUnit contains description, dependencies and acceptance mappings; Attempt pins contract/plugin/context/workspace identities; OperationReceipt binds an idempotency key to request hash and outcome; EvidenceRecord binds check definition, content snapshot, toolchain/environment and host output; CompletionProposal is a request, never a final verdict.

Keep execution lifecycle, validation outcome, and user review disposition separate. Kernel alone issues verified/unverified/blocked/failed/cancelled outcomes. An answer or draft plan may finish without code checks; implementation without required evidence finishes unverified, never verified. Required check failures return actionable feedback; explicit budgets/blockers terminate with preserved progress.

The host freezes applicable user/project checks before the first mutation. A harness can propose additional checks; weakening required criteria needs a new user-authorized contract revision. Relevant input/check-definition changes invalidate evidence. Changed implementation tests remain supported; baseline acceptance verifier definitions are stored outside plugin-owned writable content. LLM review is advisory and cannot mint passing execution evidence.

SQLite v2 has authoritative tasks/branches/runs/work_units/operations/checks/evidence/questions/review and an append-only ordered event journal; durable mutation and its event commit in one transaction. Large payloads use existing content-addressed blobs. JSONL is an export/projection, not a second authoritative writer. Plugin-emitted observations and host-generated facts retain distinct provenance.

Use a new harness-v2 directory under each existing dev/production data root, and separate v2 credential service names. Do not migrate or mutate old databases/configuration. Legacy history is read-only/export-only; no resuming old runs or automatic provider credential import. GUI/TUI use the same v2 profile.

Workspace scope is bound at task creation. Reuse verified worktree/path capabilities; direct-workspace mode captures pre-existing tracked/untracked changes. Candidate evidence hashes content (not timestamps alone); verification uses immutable input snapshots, captures dirty/new/deleted files and a pinned check definition, and records the toolchain environment. Cache reuse is within the same unchanged attempt only in v1.

Before a host side effect, persist an operation intent. Completed operations replay their stored response; mismatched idempotency inputs are rejected. Crash recovery reconciles file writes by expected hashes. Unknown shell/network/CLI outcomes are surfaced as indeterminate, never automatically re-executed. Opaque plugin checkpoints are versioned, quota-bounded and only resume the same plugin package; stale package/contract/workspace is blocked.

Cancellation revokes the run generation first, stops child/model/tool/process work, drains to terminal, then releases the task lease. Late callbacks cannot mutate state. Budgets are root-owned and inherited by children; progress and liveness are separate. Native preserves current run-budget defaults through an adapter; Codex only claims metrics enforceable by the host.

Plan/HITL and delegation are host services called by any harness, not Native-only flags. Host validates Plan ownership/revision/dependencies and gates code-work completion on required evidence. Questions persist before suspension and answers resume idempotently. Children inherit permissions and budget; parents cannot finalize while uncollected child work is live. Review reuses baseline-aware changes and journaled inverse merge; no global reset-hard recovery.

RuntimeProfile is explicit and constructed before opening any service: GUI passes its current build flavor; TUI/service take --profile, with developer launchers selecting development and packaged binaries production. No Tauri feature inference inside runtime. Profile paths and v2 credential service names are resolved in T05 prerequisites; clients discover the same daemon by profile identity.

One OS profile lock prevents competing daemons; only the lock owner runs recovery. Also take user-wide OS workspace write locks keyed by canonical directory file identity, so different profiles cannot concurrently write the same physical workspace. Distinct managed worktrees have distinct content locks; Git metadata mutations additionally serialize by repository common_dir. If an old process might still write, persist a blocked/indeterminate barrier and do not acquire a new write run.

Guardian ownership is explicit: Windows managed run trees use kill-on-close Job Objects with assignment before child execution; Unix guardians monitor daemon pipe EOF, own child process groups and TERM/KILL them on owner loss. Store daemon instance nonce and PID/start identity plus process-group/job metadata. Reboot or recovery must verify termination, never act on PID alone; inability to prove termination blocks writes. This is lifecycle containment of trusted processes, not a malicious-plugin sandbox.

Candidate manifests include tracked files, non-ignored untracked files, deletions, executable modes and explicitly declared ignored/submodule inputs. Copy all bytes into blobs, verify a second live manifest equals the captured input before accepting the candidate, materialize only from those blobs, and re-check live content at completion. Undeclared required submodule/ignored/outside-workspace input yields unavailable, not verified.

CheckDefinition separates pinned acceptance-control files from candidate implementation/dependency files. Store control file bytes and entrypoint digest outside plugin write scope, run entrypoints directly instead of resolving candidate-redefinable npm script names, and record allowed source roots, dependency manifests/lockfiles, runtime/toolchain versions and declared external inputs. Rust/TS reference checks have frozen harness entrypoints; ordinary candidate tests may change and are supplementary evidence unless covered by the frozen acceptance controls.

Verification materialization uses a private directory per candidate; candidate dependency manifests/lockfiles are preserved. Standard v1 preparation uses Cargo --locked and npm ci --ignore-scripts in that directory, with caches keyed by lockfile+toolchain and host-authorized network/process policy. Required lifecycle hooks or additional inputs require an explicit project check profile; otherwise check unavailable. Preparation stdout/exit and any environment gaps are evidence. Never borrow mutable node_modules/target from the user's live workspace.

LegacyReader opens source SQLite with READ_ONLY, never Database::open/MigrationManager/SettingsService; starts a read transaction and uses SQLite online backup into v2 temporary storage for coherent WAL-aware querying/export. JSONL export freezes byte boundaries and includes complete records only, marking live exports with capture boundaries. If safe read-only WAL access is unavailable, return a clear close-old-app/export-needed state; never use immutable=1 against a live WAL DB. Test source DB/WAL/config/JSONL contents unchanged (normal lock bookkeeping is not product-data migration).

Main paired evaluation compares the same Harness/model/config baseline vs v2, or two strategies of the same v2 Harness. Cross-Native/Codex comparisons are separate exploratory reports; missing model/version/usage/cost facts remain unavailable. CI uses deterministic conformance and task fixtures as hard gates.

Cross-profile writer coordination has a durable user-wide barrier in addition to OS locks. Guardians retain the physical workspace lock while effects can run; barriers record process groups/owner-start identities before execution and remain until termination is confirmed. A newly available lock alone never proves an orphan stopped.

v1 verification caches reuse checksummed dependency downloads only (Cargo registry/npm package tarballs), never candidate build/test outputs or mutable target/node_modules. A source/build-script change always builds and verifies anew.
product: Native implements multi-turn tools, stream/caching/compaction, Plan/HITL, steer/queue/branch, optional reviewer and cross-harness delegation via host services. Codex implements its App Server flow with approvals/questions/steer/cancel, child delegation and external thread checkpoint references; unsupported external capabilities are explicit.

Desktop and TUI share TaskView/EventEnvelope/PluginCatalog services. Provide install/enable/disable/remove/details, task Harness choice, version/control-capability display, validation evidence and recovery actions. Plugin UI is declarative data rendered by host components; no arbitrary HTML/JS contribution.

Retain core coding workflow plus current file/search/Git/Shell/MCP/skills/attachments and explicit memory context service. Autonomous memory learning, advanced marketplace, remote sandbox scheduling and arbitrary UI plugins are subsequent projects.
